beat_player.text: A fine day of steel, {player}. I lost {troop_count} good men to that flank, but I would not have had it any other way :)
Those {troop_count} men were my own doing, not yours, {player}. Come find me on the road and I will show you where I went wrong :)
Well struck, {player}. Your flank came round faster than I expected, and I have not forgotten the last time a line held like that. Pull up a stool by my fire sometime, friend :)
{player} took {gold} from my purse today and I still call it a fair lesson :) Crap, I should have guarded the ford.

beat_by_player.text: Well done, {player}. I brought {troop_count} men and went home with a lesson in humility, the cheapest thing I buy :)
Hold still, {player}, and I will show you where your left flank was thin. Old habits from the first war :)
Hell of a fight, {player}. I will remember that charge longer than you will, and I say that with respect. Till the next field, then :)
Lost {troop_count} men to {player} this afternoon. Damn good tactics, and I have seen three server resets of tactics :)

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work at the crossing, {player}. {troop_count} of us held the line and not one broke. Lovely :)
Keep your shield high, {player}. The fens taught me that rule, and the first war taught me to keep it after. Glad you were at my side today.
Shields up on the ridge, everyone. {enemy_faction} will test us again soon, so keep your {troop_count} in line :)

released_by_player.text: You let me walk free, {player}, when a ransom would have filled your purse. That is the mark of a good soul, and I will not forget it :)
Three cheers for {player}, who let an old veteran go without a single coin asked. Mercy is rarer on this road than gold :)
Released without ransom, {player}. Noted. I owe you a meal by the fire, and I have a feeling you will not let me forget it :)
{player} released me rather than ransom me. A strange choice from a rival, but I will take the freedom and keep an eye on your roads :)

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}! Our banners are a little braver with you in the ranks. Ask me anything on the road :)
I am glad you swore to {my_faction}, {player}. Come find me when you have your bearings and I will show you the good campsites :)
{player} has joined {my_faction}. We will see what kind of soldier they make, though I suspect they will do well enough :)
So you have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. Very well. Prove that oath on the field and I will have no complaint to make :)

player_granted_fief.text: Well earned, {player}! {fief} has been in worse hands, and I suspect it will be in better ones now. Hold it well :)
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. I cheered when the word came through, and I mean it. Come by when the walls need mending :)

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}! It warms my old bones to see you on the road. {persona} of {my_faction}, at your service :)
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here, riding a little slower than I used to. Mind the ruts on this stretch.
{player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, and I will be frank: our paths have crossed in ill temper before. Let us keep our swords sheathed today, shall we :)
Well met, {player}! I have ridden this road since the first war and still do not tire of the sight of a good party. {persona}, {my_faction}, pleased to see you.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, {player}. Keep your torches lit in the fens and your ranks tight on the moor. Until the next crossing :)
Fare well, {player}. The road is long and the weather is turning, so mind yourself out there.
Off you go then, {player}. I will not chase you today, but I will not forget that charge either :)
Go well, {player}. If you find yourself in trouble near the old bridge, send word and I will ride out myself :)

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. Mud in the boots, but the bread is still warm at the inn, so I call that a fair trade :)
Anyone heading out past {village} this evening? The fens are quiet, but do bring a lantern, friends. The mist is thick tonight.
Lag on the eastern road again. Patience, all. I remember when a single messenger took a full night to reach the gate :)
Still thinking of the night a lone rookie held Ganteil's bridge against the whole column. Some stories are worth telling twice :)

player_big_defeat.text: Tough day for {player}, losing {troop_count} men. Chin up, friend. I have lost whole banners and still found my way back to the fire :)
Hard luck, {player}. I heard about the {troop_count} you lost. Come find me and I will share the lessons from my own dark days :)
{player} took a heavy blow today. Those {troop_count} men will be back in the ranks soon enough, if you keep them close.
I heard you lost {troop_count} men, {player}. Do not take it personally. The field humbles the proud, and I speak from experience :)
